The defining morphologic clue is a central keratin-filled plug/crater and a size of ~2 cm. This presentation is classic for keratoacanthoma — a rapidly growing, crateriform, keratin-containing tumor of older, sun-damaged skin. Differential includes crateriform squamous cell carcinoma (well-differentiated SCC) and other crateriform lesions (e.g., inflamed epidermal inclusion cyst, nodular BCC), but the combination of rapid onset over weeks, dome-shaped architecture, central keratin plug, typical size, and location strongly favor keratoacanthoma. Because keratoacanthoma and well-differentiated SCC can be histologically and clinically similar, definitive distinction requires biopsy/excision; however, the single most likely clinical diagnosis is keratoacanthoma.

[DIAGNOSIS] Keratoacanthoma (probable)
